text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Hafez al-Assad congratulates King Hassan and Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov on Moroccan and Bulgarian national days.
- France refutes Israeli allegations that Paris is biased to Arabs and stresses balanced policy in the Middle East.
- Yemen says statements on contacts with Israel are groundless.
- Jordanian parties in demonstration held to show support to Syria praise Damascus' stands in the Middle East peace process.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ignores Arab and international denunciatons and announces Jerusalem as Israel's eternal capital.
- Syrian Peoples Assembly (parliament) listens to the government's answers about economic and foreign trade issues.
- Oman cancels Israel's participation in the waters' conference.
- Iraqi businessman invests in medical industry in Syria.
- Vice President Abdel-Halim Khaddam carries a letter from Assad to Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi over the situation in the region and developments of the peace process.
- The U.S., Turkey and Israel unite intelligence activities in the Middle East.
- The state-owned Syrian Arab Medical Establishment (Tamico) approves a production plan worth 1.6 billion Syrian pounds for 1997.
